description:
Establish a mathematically general, field-generic BCH construction and encoding stack with hardened binary decoding, researcher-oriented APIs, formally verified foundations, and benchmark-backed CPU performance.

## Background

The BCH surface accepts redundant parameters, permits mathematically inconsistent constructions, embeds binary and primitive narrow-sense assumptions, and exposes bit-specific encoding and matrix traits. The binary decoder returns message bits without a structured correction outcome or post-correction validity contract. General BCH construction also requires a reusable relationship between a base field and its splitting field, which gf2-core does not presently express as one canonical abstraction.

The target architecture uses a canonical `BchSpec` construction description, common-case convenience constructors, generic derived-code wrappers, field-generic code traits, and specialized binary representations. It supports explicit and automatically selected field representations while deriving every dependent parameter. Generalized decoding and new GPU encoding are separate follow-up work.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: gf2-core exposes one canonical relative finite-field extension abstraction covering base-field embedding, checked membership and restriction, relative degree, relative Frobenius, field-order relationships, and reusable validation certificates. Derivation of elements of exact multiplicative order $n$ and minimal polynomials over an arbitrary base field are reusable gf2-core capabilities rather than BCH-private code.

- [hard] REQ-02: Arbitrary polynomial quotient extensions are available in both compile-time configured and runtime-configured forms; runtime construction completely validates irreducibility; automatic construction is deterministic and reproducible, preferring canonical Conway polynomials where they are defined and otherwise using a documented deterministic verified irreducible-polynomial search; compile-time and runtime forms of the same field are observably equivalent and share one stable field identity; and unsupported materialization beyond `usize`/`u128` limits returns a typed error.

- [hard] REQ-03: One canonical `BchSpec` model and construction path supports primitive narrow-sense codes, primitive codes with arbitrary first root, non-primitive lengths with either a derived canonical element of order $n$ or an explicitly supplied $n$-th root of unity, arbitrary root seed sets whose $q$-cyclotomic closure the construction derives, and explicitly supplied generator polynomials; convenience constructors delegate to that path and accept only independent mathematical inputs.

- [hard] REQ-04: Construction derives the generator polynomial, dimension $k$, a witnessed classical BCH distance bound, and the correction radius that bound implies; validates $\gcd(n,q)=1$, exact root order, base/splitting-field compatibility, coefficient restriction, and $g(x)\mid x^n-1$; supports mathematically valid full-space and zero-dimensional boundary codes; and reports invalid inputs through typed errors rather than panics or silent coercion. Every new public construction, transformation, matrix, serialization, and decoding surface follows the same typed-error contract, reserving panics for violated internal invariants.

- [hard] REQ-05: Shortening and puncturing are generic linear-code transformations over arbitrary coordinate sets, one-symbol extension adds the coordinate making the total symbol sum zero, and every transformation preserves an explicit coordinate map to its mother code, derives its resulting dimension by rank, and reports the resulting information-set structure rather than assuming the mother code's systematic positions.

- [hard] REQ-06: Shared block-code, encoding, generator-matrix, and parity-check interfaces are generic over the code symbol field and representation; static generic code types provide zero-cost dispatch, runtime/type-erased handles support exploratory workflows, and binary specializations retain packed `BitVec` and `BitMatrix` behavior.

- [hard] REQ-07: General BCH encoding operates over every supported base field, provides allocating convenience methods plus allocation-free single and reusable-workspace batch methods, uses coordinate $i\leftrightarrow x^i$ internally, presents `[message | parity]` as the default systematic user layout through an explicit coordinate mapping, and permits declared standards-specific layouts.

- [hard] REQ-08: Generator and parity-check matrices remain compact until requested, support caller-provided materialization buffers and explicit opt-in caching, and use field-generic matrices with packed binary specialization. Canonical matrix serialization carries field identity and element representation, uses checksummed payloads and atomic replacement, and need not preserve byte compatibility with the existing `BitMatrix` format. Saved matrices load back to equal matrices, and loading validates field identity, element representation, and checksums, reporting any mismatch as a typed error.

- [hard] REQ-09: The binary BCH decoder uses the canonical construction model and returns typed `NoErrors`, `Corrected`, or `Uncorrectable` outcomes where `Uncorrectable` means the bounded-distance procedure found no verified correction, never a claim about the transmitted word; verifies candidate corrections; documents the exact bounded-distance guarantee and possible beyond-radius miscorrection; provides a no-allocation status/count fast path and opt-in correction-position evidence; and preserves behaviorally equivalent HIP syndrome/decode support. Decoding of nonbinary and derived codes is outside this epic.

- [hard] REQ-10: Superseded BCH constructors, redundant parameters, duplicated polynomial operations, and parallel BCH-specific abstractions are removed at cutover. BCH and its direct consumers migrate immediately; other code families may use one named, versioned compatibility boundary with a tracked removal condition.

- [hard] REQ-11: Shared property and conformance suites cover construction, encoding, matrices, shortening/puncturing/extension transformations including their coordinate maps and derived dimensions, and valid edge cases over base fields of forms $\mathrm{GF}(2)$, $\mathrm{GF}(p)$, and $\mathrm{GF}(p^r)$; representative binary and nonbinary results agree with at least two independent external oracles and with authoritative published or standards vectors where available.

- [hard] REQ-12: An approved formal-proof sketch names the exact production paths, lemma statements, and proof strategies for extension embedding/restriction and relative-Frobenius laws, quotient reduction, cyclotomic closure, generator base-field/root correctness, and systematic encoding correctness; the resulting Lean proofs and extraction-compatible refinement evidence pass the repository proof gates without untracked assumptions.

- [hard] REQ-13: A reproducible survey selects the strongest available external baselines for large-batch encoding and generator-matrix materialization. Committed benchmark receipts from suitable uncontended hosts demonstrate no statistically measurable throughput regression on existing optimized binary paths, deterministic results across supported worker counts, and tested scalar fallback for AVX2 dispatch.

- [aspirational] REQ-14: On the survey’s predeclared representative workloads, the optimized AVX2 implementation outperforms the strongest selected external implementation for large-batch encoding and generator-matrix materialization.

- [hard] REQ-15: Researcher-oriented rustdoc and runnable examples cover concise primitive binary construction, fully explicit nonbinary general construction, systematic encoding, matrix materialization and saving, coordinate conventions, error contracts, complexity, and performance-path selection.

- [hard] REQ-16: Separate tracked follow-up issues define generalized/nonbinary decoding, decoding of shortened/punctured/extended codes, and GPU encoding against the canonical interfaces established here.

## Notes

Repeated-root codes with characteristic-dividing lengths are outside scope. `BchSpec` does not require stable serialization in this epic, and matrix files deliberately contain no BCH-specific metadata. Performance evidence targets throughput rather than peak memory or allocation counts.
